newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea president stesses battle against inflation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea president stesses battle against inflation.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam said on Monday the battle against inflation would be the top economic priority next year.
"Inflationary pressure is mounting while the economy is slowing down," he said in a speech delivered to the National Assembly by Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung.
"The top priority in next year's economic policies will be placed on price stability," he said, echoing frequent pronouncements by economic officials.

The consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.7 percent during the first nine months of this year compared with a 4.7 percent rise for all of 1995 and a target for the whole of 1996 of 4.5 percent, according to official figures.
Kim said economic conditions were worsening. The current account deficit was widening and inflation was putting upward pressure on wages and land prices.
The current account deficit rose to $15.2 billion for the first eight months of this year, compared with $7.3 billion a year earlier, according to the central bank, Bank of Korea.
"Low-efficiency and high-costs have weakened the economic structure over the years, sapping the nation's competitiveness," Kim said.
He said the government will cut staffing in the state sector to improve productivity.
"The government will economise on the state budget and promote the privatisation programme as scheduled," Kim said.
The government has said private companies would be allowed to compete with the state-owned corporations such as the power monopoly Korea Electric Power Corp.
Kim said the government would try to bring down high wages, interest rates and distribution costs -- the so-called "three highs" hobbling the economy.
"The government will take the initiative by freezing wage levels for senior government officials," Kim said.
"Interest rates could be lowered through management innovation in the financial sector," he said.
"The government will expand support for small companies to help their restructuring efforts," Kim said.
He said the government planned to spend more than 10 trillion won ($12 billion) next year to improve the nation's infrastructure. (Conversion: 1$ = 828 won)
